name: slow-first-token
note: A deliberately short delay standing in for a long one. A cold model on a loaded laptop can take tens of seconds to first token, so a client with a cloud-shaped 30s timeout reports a failure that is really just patience. Kept short so the suite stays fast; the timeout value is what matters, not the wait. Repeats on exhaustion because a client-side timeout does not un-consume the turn server-side: the request arrived, the stub answered slowly, and the client stopped listening. A retry must therefore find the same slow response waiting, which is also how a genuinely slow machine behaves.
